THE ARTICULATION AGREEMENT BELOW IS SUBJECT TO PERIODIC REVISION. PLEASE CONSULT A COUNSELOR EVERY SEMESTER TO OBTAIN CURRENT INFORMATION ABOUT POSSIBLE CHANGES IN THE AGREEMENT.


Admissions and Transfer Information


Academic Advising

It is recommended students meet with an advisor each semester.


Minimum Grade of C

All courses counted toward the major, including preparation for the major courses, must be completed with a letter grade of C (2.0) or better. Credit/No Credit grading is not accepted.


Language Proficiency Requirement

For some majors, students must meet a second-language proficiency requirement. This is satisfied with the first semester of an intermediate language or demonstrating proficiency in a language other than English. For details on how to satisfy this requirement, please refer to Language Proficiency Requirement.

Area of Focus

Students must fulfill the Area of Focus requirement by selecting and completing a 15-16 unit module of coursework clustered around one of the seven K-8 subject areas. The Area of Focus allows students to gain greater appreciation of the development of a given academic field, from basic concepts and methods to more advanced applications and theoretical horizons. Courses taken to satisfy the Area of Focus may not be used to satisfy Integrative, Arts or Multicultural Studies requirements, however, Areal of Focus coursework may also be applied toward completion of a minor (an official declaration of the minor must be filed with Registration and Records).


Please see the 25-26 Catalog for more information.

Liberal Studies (LBST) provides the best preparation and content knowledge for those interested in K-8 teaching, as well as satisfying the subject matter competence state requirement for Multiple Subject. This means that students who graduate from CSUSM with a LBST degree in Elementary Subject Matter (ESM) do not have to take the Multiple Subject California Subject Examination for Teachers (CSETs) I-III. In addition, students who earn a GPA of 2.67 or higher will earn the Multiple Subject CSET I-III Waiver. The Waiver will certify students’ high level of preparation for K-8 teaching. Click on the link for more information. Those not interested in teaching will benefit from gaining a broad multidisciplinary education leading to success in a wide range of careers. These requirements address the seven core subject matter areas of the K-8 curriculum, as specified by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CCTC). Because of the considerable curricular breadth required by the state-specified ESM content preparation standards, many of the required lower-division courses also meet CSUSM’s General Education requirements. Because these GE requirements were specifically selected to meet state-specified content standards, there are very limited substitution options in the curriculum. Therefore, DO NOT FOLLOW THE Cal-GETC REQUIREMENTS; THE LOWER DIVISION LIBERAL STUDIES PREP FULFILLS THE CSU LOWER DIVISION GENERAL EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS.
